system: Current date and time: Wednesday, 18 March 2026, 06:30 (Europe/Athens, UTC+02:00).

messages.content: How did I sleep last night?

content.text:
You slept **6 h 15 min**, and Garmin gave it a **sleep score of 74 ("Fair")**.

**Last night (Tue 17 → Wed 18 March)**
- **Time:** about 23:11 to 05:52, so 6 h 41 min in bed
- **Awake time:** 26 minutes, in one stretch
- **Sleep stages:**
  - Deep: 1 h 10 min (19%)
  - Light: 3 h 45 min (60%)
  - REM: 1 h 20 min (21%)
- **Average stress while asleep:** 14, which is low and means you rested well
- **Overnight HRV:** 58 ms
- **Blood oxygen (SpO₂):** 95% on average, lowest 88%

**Compared with the night before**, last night was better:

| | Mon → Tue | Tue → Wed |
|---|---|---|
| Score | 63 | **74** |
| Sleep | 5 h 42 min | **6 h 15 min** |
| Times you woke up | 2 | **1** |
| Stress while asleep | 19 | **14** |
| HRV | 61 ms | 58 ms |

**My take:** The quality was good. Your deep sleep and REM made up a healthy share of the night, and your stress stayed low. Length is the main problem: at about 6¼ hours, you're short of the 7–9 hours most adults need. That's probably why the score is only "Fair." Garmin only has data for these two nights, so I can't compare against a longer stretch. Both nights were under 6½ hours, though, so you may be building up a sleep shortfall. Going to bed 30–45 minutes earlier would likely help more than anything else.

I can also check today's training readiness or Body Battery to see how recovered you are.
